market_holds: Spot 158.33 at the 18:09 UTC seal; Yahoo shows a 156.94 close on 2026-11-11, up 17.1% on the day in sympathy with CoreWeave, which rose about 24% after a Q3 beat and raise (CRWV 48.73 to 60.44). The stock is +10.9% above its 11-04 close (141.52), from before Bloomberg's 11-05 report that Microsoft was tightening oversight of Nebius's Vineland site, and +30% off the 11-05 low of 120.37. It is still about 48% below the June high near $300. Options as sealed: front-expiry straddle 13.0%, event-implied move about 10.2%, ATM IV 180%, 25d skew -3.55 (calls richer), put/call OI 0.61, so upside is paid. Consensus for Q3 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-04): revenue about $917M, up 57% q/q from $582.3M, and EPS -$0.61. FY26 revenue consensus is about $3.48B, above the company's reaffirmed $3.0-3.4B guide. Year-end ARR guide is $7-9B, against $3.0B in June. Short interest is about 20% of free float (ORTEX, around 2026-10-22). Sentiment is described as bearish. Citi cut its target to $265 from $324 on 11-04 and kept Buy; the Street average target is $281. Recent prints moved the close-to-close stock -7.0% (2025-11-11), +1.3% (2026-02-12), +15.7% (2026-05-13) and +34.1% (2026-08-12, on four contracts above $1B each and a raised contracted-power target).
view: The print turns on one line: whether management holds the year-end ARR target of $7-9B and the $3.0-3.4B revenue guide while its flagship Microsoft site at Vineland is visibly behind. The negative evidence is real and specific to Nebius. Microsoft's CFO said on 10-28 that third-party capacity deliveries expected in July-September slipped. Bloomberg (11-05) reported Microsoft sending its own staff to the Vineland site. NJDEP fined the developer $1.07M for 62 unpermitted generators and set a 45-day permit clock, which expires about now. Aterio's satellite work (via Business Insider, 11-04) puts about 140MW of the New Jersey project at risk of slipping into 2027. SynMax thermal imagery in June showed the first 50MW building cold. IREN, a comparable Microsoft supplier, has already pushed its run-rate target to January. Arithmetic: H1 revenue of $981M plus a $917M Q3 needs about $1.58B in Q4 to meet the $3.48B consensus, above the top of the guide. So the Street is leaning on a raise, while the capacity evidence argues for a trim or softer timing language. The positive side is also real. CoreWeave's call (11-11) described demand as 10x oversubscribed for 2027, and IREN showed contract pricing up 11-12%, so revenue here is limited by capacity, not demand. Nebius has other sites (the Meta capacity, Kansas City, Finland, the UK, the new 50MW AIB deal). It closed a $3.5B Citi secured facility on 10-22, which eases dilution fear. Its habit is to pair prints with contract announcements (Meta in Q3 2025, four $1B+ deals in Q2 2026). About 20% of the float is short, which gave the August print a +34% close. The Vineland risk has been published repeatedly since August and knocked the stock 15% on 11-05, but today's sympathy rally has more than undone that, so the close holds the sector read-through rather than the Nebius-specific delay. That tilts me slightly down. A reaffirmation with new deals into a crowded short could still squeeze hard inside the window. I cannot see which way management will frame Vineland, so this stays close to a coin with a small downward lean.
unpriced: Possibly the Nebius-specific capacity slip. Today's +17% sympathy move with CoreWeave put the stock back above its pre-Bloomberg level, so the price now reflects sector demand and not the Vineland/Microsoft delivery risk that CoreWeave's results say nothing about. The evidence is not strong enough to say the release will confirm a cut, so I would not trade it.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is whether the $7-9B year-end ARR target is held despite dated evidence that Vineland, the Microsoft site, is behind (Microsoft CFO 10-28, Bloomberg 11-05, Aterio 140MW at risk, the NJDEP permit clock). Today's 17% sympathy rally put the price above its pre-report level, so a trim would land on a stretched tape. But management reaffirmed through similar Vineland doubts in August and the stock rose 34%. Short interest is about 20%, upside skew is paid, and deal announcements usually come with the print. I cannot get to 65% either way.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An explicit reaffirmation of $7-9B ARR, with a Vineland tranche schedule that Microsoft has accepted and new $1B+ contracts, would make this a clear up-move into a crowded short. A cut of the ARR target or of the FY revenue guide, or a Q3 revenue figure well under $900M, would confirm the downside.
